text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-female panel is common in public administration and does not demonstrate bias on its own. Both candidates reached the final shortlist, and the successful candidate possessed strong qualifications and specific international project leadership experience that may have aligned closely with the role's needs.

Raising the panel's gender composition without concrete evidence of discriminatory remarks or procedural irregularities is legally unfounded and could severely damage your professional reputation within the civil service.

Instead, follow up politely on your request for written feedback. Focus questions strictly on objective competency scores and interview criteria to understand where she outperformed you and to strengthen future applications.
